title: Choose the visual world for mufasil.site
question: The roll assigned Truck Art Tailgate. Keep it, take my pick or an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Truck Art Tailgate
options.lineage: Pakistani truck art, the hand-painted Bedford lorries of Karachi
options.thesis: A backend is the truck that carries the load; this one is painted like it is proud of it.
options.viewport: The tailgate is the hero: name hand-lettered in a framed panel, role on a painted ribbon, CV and project actions as chrome plaques, code and stack in inset panels.
options.risk: Can tip into souvenir kitsch if the panels crowd; must still read as a senior engineer in five seconds.

raised.raise: Every panel is numbered and named, so the page reads as one sequence.
Facts are set as measured tabular figures: 11+ years, 19+ engineers, 4 months.
One quiet unpainted field around the primary actions keeps the ornament from swallowing them.

options.label: Status Page
options.lineage: service status pages engineers check every day
options.thesis: His career as a production status page: operational since 2014.
options.viewport: A status header reading operational, name and role, components such as Node.js, AWS and Team leadership with a bar per real year, and Download CV beside Start a project.
options.risk: A familiar developer joke; the bars may only map real years and roles, never invented uptime numbers.

options.label: Night Instrument Panel
options.lineage: a small aircraft's six-pack of night instruments
options.thesis: Six calm instruments, each holding one true fact a hiring manager cross-checks.
options.viewport: Name and role above two rows of three dials: years, team led, certification, time zone, availability, current role.
options.case: Fuses well for engineers who live in dashboards; weaker for recruiters, since most of his facts are not quantities.
options.risk: Dials for non-numbers feel forced, and a cockpit can read as a theme rather than a person.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.thesis: A fix explained the way a friend sketches it on a napkin.
options.viewport: A marker headline over a doodled diagram of one fix.
options.case: Engineers love it, but it undercuts the senior, high-end read recruiters need.
options.risk: Reads junior or playful for a tech lead.
options.kept: Explain one real fix step by step instead of claiming expertise.

options.label: Merz Collage
options.thesis: A career as a found object of tickets and type.
options.viewport: Scraps pinned at angles around his name.
options.case: No link to backend work; hurts five-second clarity.
options.risk: Chaos where a hiring manager wants order.
options.kept: Confident scale contrast: one huge element, many small ones.

options.label: Lotería Night
options.thesis: Skills as a deck of named, numbered cards.
options.viewport: A tabla grid of skill cards.
options.case: Not his cultural home, and a game frame weakens the offer.
options.risk: Borrowed culture with no tie to the work.
options.kept: Every item named and numbered in the same breath.

options.label: Forge Floor
options.lineage: a blacksmith drawing iron under a power hammer
options.thesis: Shipping under pressure, one blow at a time.
options.viewport: A glowing bar lengthening with each project.
options.case: Strong energy, but heavy and literal; clarity suffers.
options.kept: Facts measured like chalk marks, in tabular figures.

options.label: Ikebana Alcove
options.lineage: a tokonoma alcove with one arrangement
options.thesis: Restraint where emptiness does the work.
options.viewport: One line of text in a quiet alcove.
options.case: Too quiet for a page that must make two offers fast.
options.kept: Charged empty space around the one thing that matters.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer portfolio, executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role beside a photo, an availability badge, a CV button and a row of stats.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from hundreds of developer portfolios by design.
